The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Allahabad High Court questions order for judicial probe into caste discrimination at NLU Prayagraj
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has questioned a single-judge's order directing a judicial probe into caste discrimination allegations against Dr Deepak Sharma, the Head of the Department of Law, Dr. Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLU) [ Dr Deepak Sharma v State of UP And 5 Others ]. A Bench of Justice Siddhartha Varma and Justice Kunal Ravi Singh said there was no occasion to order a judicial inquiry when an Equal Opportunity Cell is already in place at the university. "Even if the allegations are of a serious nature, the power of the University to examine such allegations through an appropriately constituted Equal Opportunity Cell ought not to have been taken away, as it is within the domain of the University to look into the welfare of the students and deal with situations as they arise," the Court said. However, considering that the inquiry report was required to be submitted by September 24, the Court said the same be placed before it in a sealed cover on September 29, if it has been already prepared. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on September 28 granted interim protection from arrest to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member Gaurav Bharti in connection with an first information report (FIR) registered against him for filming the dilapidated condition of a government primary school in Farrukhabad [ Gaurav Bharti @ Gaurav Kumar v. State of U.P. and 3 Others] . A Division Bench comprising Justice Salil Kumar Rai and Padam Narain Mishra issued the direction on petition filed by Bharti seeking the quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against him. "The petitioner shall not be arrested in pursuance of the First Information Report dated 19.08.2026, registered as Case Crime No. 0246 of 2026, under Sections 352 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station- Nawabganj, District Fatehgarh," the Court directed. The controversy stemmed from an FIR registered on August 19 at Nawabganj Police Station in Fatehgarh district. According to the FIR, the petitioner was accused of having "illegally prepared a video of the institution and had misrepresented the condition of the institution." items.title: Delhi High Court to decide personality rights cases of 3 celebrities together
items.summary: Considering the increasing number of suits seeking protection of personality rights, the Delhi High Court on Monday said it would first hear three specific suits to consider the scope and contours of such rights. The three suits have been filed by actors Vivek Oberoi and Janhvi Kapoor and Amitabh Bachchan’s granddaughter Aaradhya Bachchan. While explaining the rationale behind prioritizing these cases, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani said, "The way I look at it is that there is this monolithic block of clay or wood in front of me that makes no sense to me. I don't discern any design or image. I want to chip off what I consider is not personality right. Whatever remains, remains. Subsequently other matters may come up, that would require the court chip off further part so that ultimately some kind of a definitive face emerges saying that this is what personality rights is about." Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani During the hearing, the Court made a light-hearted remark about prayers for takedown of fan accounts in the personality rights suits filed by actors. items.title: Three-language policy: Supreme Court directs CBSE to grant class 6 same exemption allowed to class 7
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to extend the exemption granted to students of classes VII, VIII and IX under the three-language formula to Class VI students as well [Yashica Bhandari Jain & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.]. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana overruled the Central government’s stand against the exemption. The government had said that nearly 99 percent of schools under the CBSE are ready to implement the policy. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Under the transitional framework mandated by the Court, students will continue studying the third language as part of their curriculum, but will not face a mandatory class X Board examination in the subject, nor will their final promotion or certification be stalled on account of it. The direction was passed in a batch of petitions filed by parents and teachers challenging a CBSE circular issued on May 15, 2026. items.title: Delhi High Court quizzes Meta over Instagram feature being misused to violate copyright
items.summary: The Delhi High Court today raised concerns that a feature on social media platform Instagram could be used as a tool to violate the copyrights of original content creators [ Dr Vikas Divyakirti vs Meta Platforms ]. Addressing counsel representing Meta (which owns Instagram) Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani noted that this feature allows Instagram users to make changes to reels posted by others, and re-upload a modified version. "Tell me Mr Pathak (Meta's counsel), you have a feature on Instagram that you can pick up a video, paste it and make it your own video. For example, someone is cooking a recipe, you can take the whole video and add yourself cooking as per the recipe and run it on your own handle," the Court observed. The Court stated that this Instagram feature allows manipulation and enables copyright infringement. "You are allowing manipulation. It is a tool for copyright violation. Does your platform permit this? It is proof of copyright violation. It is a mischievous feature you have got there. These are powerful tools you are creating; then you give these to a ghost. items.title: Juniors lawyers must be paid stipend: Madhya Pradesh High Court orders State Bar Council to frame guidelines
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has issued directions to ensure that junior advocates are paid a stipend for their work [Vipin Pandey v. Rani Durgavati University, Jabalpur & Ors.]. Justice Vishal Dhagat said that the bar body should ensure that young lawyers' ability to maintain a decent standard of living and have their transportation expenses covered during the initial phases of law practice. Hence, it directed the Madhya Pradesh State Bar Council to consult the High Court Bar Association and the High Court Advocates' Bar Association to formulate guidelines setting a minimum stipend for junior advocates across urban and rural areas within a strict six-month timeframe. The order was passed during the hearing of a petition where a junior counsel, appearing for the petitioner, sought an adjournment on the ground that the arguing counsel was not available. Upon being questioned by the Court, the junior counsel revealed that she was not receiving any stipend. items.title: Bombay HC asks sessions court to reconsider plea to close POCSO case against accused with mental incapacity
items.summary: The Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court recently quashed a sessions court order that had refused to discharge a 19-year-old accused in a POCSO case, despite medical evidence establishing his mental incapacity to face criminal trial. Justice Mehroz K Pathan remanded the matter back to the Additional Sessions Court in Bhandara district of Maharashtra for fresh consideration. Justice Mehroz K Pathan The accused faced prosecution for offences under the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). His lawyers filed a plea to discharge him from the case, claiming that he suffered from severe intellectual vulnerability. They argued that he could not comprehend his actions or instruct counsel. Medical tests, including a psychiatric assessment, revealed that the accused had an Intelligence Quotient below seventy and a mental age of approximately fourteen. Three doctors subsequently testified before the trial court confirming that the accused suffered from mild intellectual disability and was unfit to stand trial. items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider framing rules to regulate social media accounts of minors
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Central government to examine whether statutory rules can be put in place to ensure that social media platforms comply with Indian law governing contracts entered into by minors. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed by NGO Just Rights for Children Alliance seeking safeguards for children below eighteen years who access social media and other digital platforms. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The petition was filed raising concerns over minors independently creating social media accounts by accepting the terms of service of digital platforms despite Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act rendering minors incompetent to contract. The petition said there should be age-verification mechanisms, parental consent requirements and other safeguards for minors accessing digital platforms, rather than a complete prohibition on their access to the internet. items.title: Collegium recommends 3 new judges for Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the names of 3 High Court Chief Justices for elevation to the apex court. Those recommended to be appointed as judges of the top court are: 1. Justice Sunita Agarwal , Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court. 2. Justice DK Upadhyay , Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. 3. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh , Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. Justice Agarwal, who is originally a judge of the Allahabad High Court, has been the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court since July 2023. She graduated in law from Awadh University in 1989 and has been in the legal profession since December 1990. She was appointed as a judge in November 2011. Once elevated to the top court, she will retire in April 2031. Justice Singh studied law at the University of Delhi and enrolled as an advocate in 1990. He practiced before the Patna High Court from 1990 to 2000 and then before the Jharkhand High Court till elevation as its judge in 2012. He was the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court from December 20, 2022 and February 19, 2023. items.title: Delhi High Court seeks response from Delhi Police on Sharjeel Imam's plea to access PhD study material in jail
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday sought responses from the Tihar Jail authorities and Delhi Police on a plea by JNU scholar and Delhi riots accused Sharjeel Imam seeking permission to access research material stored on a pen drive and use prison computers for his PhD work. Justice Sanjeev Narula directed that that the responses should be filed in four weeks. Advocate Ahmad Ibrahim appeared for Imam and argued that Imam has been in custody since January 2020. "At the time of his arrest, he was in the final year of his PhD. His synopsis has been approved by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the University [JNU]. I am asking that he be allowed his research material," Ibrahim said. He added that Imam was not seeking access to the internet but only the computer systems available in jail. When the Bench asked him why physical copies of the study material cannot be supplied to Imam, Ibrahim said that it would run into lakhs of pages. Imam enrolled as a doctoral scholar in Modern History at Jawaharlal Nehru University before his arrest in January 2020. items.title: Sohrabuddin case: Supreme Court says it will not reopen Amit Shah's discharge but seeks CBI reply on plea against acquittal of others
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice on an appeal challenging the acquittal of all 22 accused, including 21 police personnel, in the case registered on allegations that Sohrabuddin Shaikh, his wife Kauser Bi and associate Tulsiram Prajapati were killed in a fake encounter by the Gujarat police. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought the response of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) which investigated the matter, as well as the 22 persons who were acquitted in the case. Notably, the Court clarified that Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s 2014 discharge from the case will not be reopened. “ We hope that you are not assailing paragraph 43 (of a Bombay High Court judgment which rejected an application questioning Shah's discharge) or reopening a discharge that has become final (by an order passed by the Supreme Court ), ” said Justice Bagchi. CJI Kant agreed. “We would like to see some of the witnesses statements … as far as the acquittal part is concerned. items.title: J&K High Court orders action against man who wasted court's time with plea to trace non-existent daughter
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently ordered that a criminal complaint be filed against a man who was found to have approached the Court in 2023 with a plea to trace the whereabouts of a daughter who did not exist. An inquiry carried on the High Court's directions by the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) at Rajouri found that the petitioner had created a fictitious daughter and accused others of confining her only to harass them and satisfy his ego and frustration. Whereas the petitioner was given several opportunities to explain his conduct, he was not able to provide any proof that the daughter he referred to in his petition was real. The petitioner, as well as his lawyer, eventually stopped appearing in the case altogether. In an order passed on September 17, Justice Sanjay Dhar observed that the petitioner had given false information not only before the police but also before the High Court, and had engaged a constitutional Court in frivolous proceedings for more than three years.
